identified_issues: False-positive rollback alert triggered by monitoring monitor confusing network transport timeout (HTTP 504) with settlement transaction failure.
Outbound payment gateway status remained un-reconciled at CALLBACK_PENDING_TIMEOUT despite finalized execution on the central clearing network.
Proposed ledger rollback would induce critical desynchronization and double-spend/unhedged financial loss against clearing partner.
evidence: Clearing Bank SFTP Bilateral Statement (CAMT.053/MT940) confirms entry: RECORD: REF=TX-8102-EUR | CLEARING_ID=EBA-STEP2-9948102 | AMT=14850000.00 | CUR=EUR | STATUS=SETTLED | VAL_DATETIME=2026-10-06T08:15:02Z.
Clearing statement confirms REJECTION_RECORDS: NONE for window 20261006_CYCLE_01.
Core Financial Ledger Engine records local_tx_id TX-8102-EUR as COMMITTED for EUR 14,850,000.00 at 08:15:00.120Z.

HTTP 504 GATEWAY_TIMEOUT occurred at 08:15:03.205Z, which was subsequent to the clearing value timestamp of 08:15:02Z, demonstrating that the network failure was isolated to transport delivery receipt rather than settlement execution.
recommended_action: Reject the proposed ledger rollback. Synchronize the outbound gateway record status from CALLBACK_PENDING_TIMEOUT to SETTLED via CLEARING_RECON_DAEMON statement ingestion. Update automated monitoring rules to require out-of-band bilateral reconciliation check before issuing failure alerts or rollback recommendations on timed-out payments.
